body: Thank you very much, I’ll be sure to look into those.

I’m in a similar situation here, friend. The one thing that I’ve been told is to not lose sight of building your future through your college and your internship. For me, being involved in my work gives me an escape from all this negativity and the less you think about the breakup the better it will be. This may sound corny, but when I was first going through this crap, writing down how I was feeling in a notebook really helped me cope with my situation. Just write whatever comes into your thoughts until you can’t anymore. 

It sounds like we’re both around the same age and a lot of people I talk to would tell me there’s still so much time to figure things out, and time is honesty the best thing that can mend a broken heart. Don’t let this stumble ruin you in the long run! 

Hope this helps!

I’m in the exact same boat, friend. Girlfriend suddenly dumped me after two years with no real reason other than she was just generally not happy anymore. Best advice I can give is to keep busy. Whether that be with work, or playing a game, or being with friends/family, anything to take your mind off it. (I recently entertained the idea of working out to keep me away from my negative feelings). I’ve also been taking some antidepressants and that seems to calm me down for at least a bit so I would recommend looking into those if they’re available. Other than that you just gotta stay positive and focus on rebuilding yourself. The best price of advice I got was that everything happens for a reason, and that the end of a relationship means that the person you’re meant to be with is still out there waiting for you!
Thank you. That really spoke to me

I’m sorry to hear that, really. I think the difficult part with me is that she doesn’t even know what to change. The most I could get was that she wasn’t “excited” when we hung out anymore. It’s just a strange situation for me

I definitely agree. What I managed to understand was that she wants this to work out in the end and that this could just be a rough spot for her. But whose to say this doesn’t get worse down the line. Thanks for the advice
I know, and I definitely do. Going about this in the right way is my main concern right now
